item.title: Kobe Harborland: The Waterfront Heart of the Port City — Guide
item.description: Kobe Harborland is the city’s waterfront playground, a redeveloped stretch of the old docks where shopping centres, restaurants and a lit Ferris wheel line the quays. Across the water in adjoining Meriken Park stand the city’s icons: the lattice-framed red Port Tower and the white steel sails of the Maritime Museum, alongside a preserved section of quay left buckled by the 1995 earthquake as a memorial. Come at dusk, when the towers, ships and mall lights double in the harbour water — it is deservedly rated among Japan’s best night views.
